environment: epic development container, shared; interleaved arms, minimum of samples

composite.what: two recognition results and one census over four golden fixtures, rebuilt each iteration
composite.budget_note: Loose because of the host, not because the code may be 40% slower. Measured repeatedly over one evening with nothing else obviously running, this two-second arm's minimum-of-five ranged 1.93s to 2.66s -- 1.38x. A ceiling under that reports the load. The census arm is fifty times longer, does not move like this, and is the tight one; this arm becomes a real budget only on a dedicated machine.

census.what: feature_census over the ten vendored NIST parts and three real gramel parts, imported once

commands: uv run python tools/benchmark_recognition.py --implementation package --workload composite --iterations 5
uv run python tools/benchmark_recognition.py --implementation package --workload census --iterations 3
uv run python tools/benchmark_recognition.py --implementation package --workload census --iterations 3 --check docs/benchmarks/recognition-budget.json
budget_note: The default multiplier, used by any workload that records none of its own. Applied to the census arm, which is long enough to be stable here.
